[2031-10-27] Dentist gave me this printed sheet, I'm gonna type it so I have it on my phone:
 Aftercare following extraction / surgical procedure

You have had a tooth removed today. Following these simple instructions will help the area heal well and reduce your chance of problems.

Bleeding: A little oozing is normal for the first 24 hours. If bleeding continues, fold a clean piece of gauze or a damp tea bag, place it over the socket and bite down firmly for 20 minutes. Do not keep checking it.

Pain: Take your usual painkillers (ibuprofen or paracetamol) as directed on the packet. Start before the numbness wears off. Do not take aspirin.

Swelling: Some swelling is expected and peaks on day two. A cold pack held to the cheek for 10 minutes on and 10 off may help. 

Eating and drinking: Today, only soft cool foods and drinks. Avoid hot drinks, alcohol and chewing on the affected side. Do not use a straw. 

Rinsing and cleaning: Do not rinse your mouth, spit or touch the area today. From tomorrow, gently rinse with warm salty water (half a teaspoon of salt in a cup of warm water) after meals. Brush your other teeth as usual, avoiding the socket.

Smoking: Please avoid smoking for as long as you can; it delays healing and raises the risk of a painful dry socket.

Exercise: Avoid strenuous exercise for 48 hours, as it can restart bleeding.

Stitches: dissolvable stitches will fall out by themselves in about a week. Your follow-up check is 10 days after the procedure; call reception to book.

If you have a fever, a bad taste, or increasing pain after day three, contact us.
